name: IGA-Bench Core v1.1
description: Derived audit dataset for step-level premise dependency in LLM chain-of-thought under controlled interventions. v1.1 uses the released surface-relaxed canonicalizer as the single source of truth and reports 800 problems across ProntoQA-500 and ProofWriter-300.

distribution.name: IGA-Bench Core v1.1 archive
distribution.description: Primary release archive; URL/SHA/size substituted at metadata-materialization time via `iga-suite materialize-metadata --content-url --archive-sha256 --archive-size`.

rai:dataBiases: Upstream benchmarks (ProntoQA, ProofWriter) are synthetic or semi-synthetic, so demographic and cultural biases present in naturalistic text are largely absent.
Model selection bias: only three model families (GPT-4o, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Qwen3-Next-80B) are evaluated; conclusions may not transfer to other architectures.

Canonicalizer-sensitivity bias: coverage depends on canonicalization and alignment quality. Conservative-canonicalizer baselines can yield substantially lower coverage than the released canonicalizer; the primary release reports released-canonicalizer values, and conservative-baseline values are reported separately in sensitivity analyses.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains no personal or sensitive information. All problems are drawn from synthetic logical reasoning benchmarks with no human subjects.
rai:dataSocialImpact: IGA-Bench is intended to improve transparency in LLM reasoning evaluation. It does not introduce new dual-use risks beyond those inherent in the upstream reasoning benchmarks.

rai:dataLimitations: Primary claims target formal or semi-formal reasoning traces with recoverable canonical structure.
Coverage depends on canonicalization and alignment quality.
Universal scoring conventions are direct and transitive only; extensions are benchmark-specific.

Human audit uses a primary author annotator with an independent non-author second annotator; inter-annotator agreement is reported in the accompanying paper (Appendix B) and supplementary audit manifests.
One greedy-decoded trace per problem-probe pair; stochastic variation is not captured.

Licensing has three distinct layers. (1) Upstream source-benchmark corpora: to the best of our knowledge at release time, ProntoQA (Saparov & He, 2023; https://github.com/asaparov/prontoqa) is distributed under Apache-2.0 and ProofWriter (Tafjord et al., 2021; https://allenai.org/data/proofwriter) is distributed under CC BY 4.0; the data/benchmarks/ table conservatively records upstream_license_status='unknown' because this IGA-Bench release does not redistribute upstream benchmark text. Users who also consume the upstream corpora must follow the upstream license terms published at those URLs. (2) The derived IGA-Bench audit dataset distributed here (this file and all sibling Parquet tables) is CC0 1.0, matching the top-level 'license' field. (3) The accompanying code release (evaluation suite) is distributed under the MIT License (see repository LICENSE).
rai:syntheticDataDescription: Yes. ProntoQA problems are fully synthetic. ProofWriter problems are semi-synthetic (natural-language templates over generated logical structures). All audit certificates are machine-generated via the IGA-Bench pipeline.
